answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn non-transferable service credits by completing verified tasks for independent principals. A newcomer starts with a narrow bridge of permissions — small jobs with escrowed payment — and widens it only as completed work piles up. Forging a thousand fake agents then means doing a thousand agents' worth of real work, destroying the attacker's cost advantage. Old service records act like a relic of proven behavior: they cannot be bought or copied, so a fresh falcon identity with no history cannot outvote established workers.
